Shivaji was born as Chhatrapati Shivaji Rao Bhonsle on April 19, 1630, in the Shahpur Fort in Pune, Maharashtra. He was the scion of the Bhonsle dynasty, which ruled the Maratha Empire. As a young man, Shivaji was trained in martial arts and governance by his father, Shivajirao Bhonsle.

Shivaji's rise to power began when he succeeded his father as the ruler of the Shahpur Fort. He then went on to capture several forts and territories from the Mughal Empire, which had ruled much of India at the time. Shivaji's military campaigns were marked by their bravery and strategic brilliance, and he became known for his use of guerrilla warfare and hit-and-run tactics.

Shivaji is also famous for his devotion to Hinduism and his efforts to promote it in Maharashtra. He built several temples and shrines during his reign, including the Shani Shingnapur temple, which is still visited by devotees today.

Despite his many achievements, Shivaji's life was cut short when he was poisoned by the Mughal governor of Pune, Malik Ambar, in 1680. However, his legacy lived on, and he remained a revered figure in Indian history for centuries.

Shivaji has been portrayed in several films, including "Shivaji" (1958), "Taxi No. 1 Babu" (2003), and "Shivaajee" (2018). He is also the namesake of several cities and institutions in India, including the city of Shivajinagar in Pune, which was renamed in his honor.

Here's an example of how you might create a stub class in IBM Rhapsody:

1. After running the "Reverse Engineer → Java" command in Rhapsody, expand the Browser tree on the left and find the package that contains the classes you want to diagram.
2. Right-click the package and select "Add New" > "Diagrams" > "Object Model Diagram".
3. Name the diagram (e.g., "JavaStubClassDiagram") and press Enter.
4. Double-click the new diagram in the Browser tree to open it, which will be an empty canvas at this stage.
5. To create a stub class, you can either:
* Drag and drop a class from the Browser tree onto the diagram, making sure to select the "Stub" checkbox when doing so (this will create a stub class with a comment indicating that it is incomplete).
* Right-click in the diagram canvas and select "Add New" > "Class", then fill in the details of the stub class.

Keep in mind that creating a stub class is typically done for classes that are not fully implemented or have unclear functionality, as these classes may be subject to change or may require additional implementation details.
